title: Algebra-sheaf quotient and underlying module cokernel with normalized projection
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings, $\mathcal B$ a commutative $\mathcal O$-algebra sheaf [def-weil-pbc-ringed-space-algebra-module], and $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal B$ an ideal subsheaf (a subsheaf whose sections on every open $U$ are an ideal of $\mathcal B(U)$). Put $\mathcal P(U)=\mathcal B(U)/\mathcal I(U)$, with induced restrictions, and let $\theta:\mathcal P\to\mathcal Q$ be its sheafification in commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Write $p:\mathcal B\to\mathcal P$ for the sectionwise quotient and $q=\theta p$. The structure map $q\sigma_{\mathcal B}$ makes $\mathcal Q$ a commutative $\mathcal O$-algebra sheaf, and $q$ an algebra morphism. Let $c:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ be the cokernel of the inclusion $\mathcal I\hookrightarrow\mathcal B$ in sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. There is a canonical module isomorphism $h:\mathcal C\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal Q$ with $hc=q$, using the module structures induced by the algebra structure maps. The map $q$ is locally surjective. For every commutative $\mathcal O$-algebra sheaf $\mathcal H$ and algebra map $\chi:\mathcal B\to\mathcal H$ that annihilates $\mathcal I$ on every open, there is exactly one algebra map $\bar\chi:\mathcal Q\to\mathcal H$ with $\bar\chi q=\chi$.

proof.text: Use the canonical sectionwise ring quotient P, its ring sheafification Q, and the projection q. Composition with the structure morphism of B equips Q with its O-algebra structure. The same ring maps are O-linear after restriction of scalars. The quotient map kills I because Ideal.Quotient.mk sends every element of I to zero, and the sheafification unit preserves zero.

source.place: Cokernel construction immediately preceding Tag 01AG, lemma-abelian; the quotient presheaf from the existing ideal-module-quotients definition

proof.text: The sheafification unit theta of P is locally surjective and locally injective on underlying sets, by the ring-sheafification result and Mathlib Presheaf.isLocallySurjective_toSheafify' / Presheaf.isLocallyInjective_toSheafify'. The sectionwise quotient projection p is surjective by Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective. Local surjectivity is closed under composition, so q = p followed by theta is locally surjective.

Regard the sectionwise quotient rings P as an O-module presheaf, by restricting scalars along O -> B -> P. The unit theta induces an O-linear map from this module presheaf to the underlying O-module of Q, with exactly the same functions on sections. It is locally bijective by the preceding step. For any O-module sheaf N and f: B -> N killing I, QuotientAddGroup.lift gives sectionwise additive maps P(U) -> N(U). Surjectivity of B(U) -> P(U) reduces naturality and O-linearity of these maps to those of f. Apply Mathlib PresheafOfModules.homEquivOfIsLocallyBijective to theta and N.isSheaf to descend this module-presheaf map uniquely to Q -> N. Its composite with q is f by the factorization p followed by theta; uniqueness follows from injectivity of the hom equivalence and sectionwise surjectivity of p. This proves the module cokernel property of the specified q directly, without computing its kernel on sections.

proof.text: Construct the CokernelCofork with projection q, its zero relation proved in step 1, and the universal property proved in step 3. The unique isomorphism between this colimit and the chosen categorical cokernel gives h. The cocone comparison equation at WalkingParallelPair.one is exactly cokernel.pi followed by h.hom = q.

source.place: Cokernel universal property in the construction preceding Tag 01AG, lemma-abelian

proof.text: For an O-algebra sheaf H and an algebra map chi: B -> H annihilating I, form a ring-presheaf map P -> H with components Ideal.Quotient.lift chi. Naturality is checked on representatives. Ring sheafification gives a ring-sheaf map phi: Q -> H, and the sheafification unit equation implies q followed by phi = chi. This identity and the algebra compatibility of chi imply the structure-map identity for phi, so phi defines an Under O morphism. For uniqueness, use sheafify_hom_ext, then check equality on each quotient representative using Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective and the assumed factorization through q.
